part1.q:
Read the passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the best answer to each of the following questions from 1 to 8.
THE RISE OF PALM PAYMENT TECHNOLOGY
Amazon One is an advanced payment method using palm recognition to identify customers. This biometric system scans both surface lines and vein patterns beneath the skin, creating a unique identification for each person. Users can register through their smartphones, connecting palm data to their accounts. Once
enrolled, they can make purchases by simply holding their hands above scanners, eliminating the need for wallets or phones. The technology promises to transform how people shop in busy environments.
Currently operating in over four hundred stores nationwide, including Whole Foods Markets, this solution extends beyond Amazon's own establishments. Various venues like sports arenas, airports, and dining
establishments have begun implementing these scanners. The corporation emphasizes speed and efficiency as primary benefits, particularly in crowded locations where traditional checkout methods create bottlenecks. Additionally, potential applications include building entry systems, membership verification, and medical
facilities, suggesting broader uses beyond retail transactions.
Nevertheless, serious concerns surround this advancement. Security experts highlight fundamental risks with biometric information storage since compromised biological data remains permanent, unlike changeable
passwords. Cloud-based storage amplifies vulnerability to cyberattacks, while questions about corporate
surveillance persist. Many consumers lack a complete understanding of future data usage, creating
transparency issues that regulatory frameworks have not adequately addressed yet.
This palm-scanning innovation reflects movement toward touchless interactions and automated services. Success depends on balancing customer convenience against privacy protection requirements. While adoption continues growing, debates about ethical implications intensify. The outcome will likely
influence how businesses handle personal identification going forward, potentially establishing precedents for biometric authentication standards across industries worldwide.
(Adapted from https://retail-innovation.com/al)
Which information is NOT MENTIONED in the passage?
options: Each palm scan takes a specific amount of time to process.
The system has been used in sports arenas and airports.
The technology scans both surface lines and vein patterns.
Users can register using their smartphones.

Read the passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the best answer to each of the following questions from 20 to 29.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) has rapidly become one of the most influential technologies of the modern era. Once limited to science fiction, AI is now integrated into daily life, from virtual assistants and recommendation systems to medical diagnosis and autonomous vehicles. Supporters argue that AI increases efficiency, reduces human error, and improves quality of life. However, critics warn that the widespread adoption of AI may create serious ethical, economic, and social challenges. The debate surrounding AI is therefore not simply about
technology itself, but about how humanity chooses to use it responsibly.
At first, AI appears to offer enormous advantages. I By automating repetitive and time-consuming tasks, AI allows humans to focus on creativity, innovation, and complex problem-solving. In healthcare, for example, AI systems can analyze medical data faster than doctors in certain situations, potentially improving patient
outcomes. Yet, despite these benefits, concerns remain about the unequal distribution of technological power. Large corporations with access to massive amounts of data may dominate industries, while smaller businesses and workers struggle to adapt to the changing economy.
Experts also disagree about AI’s long-term effect on employment. II Some believe that AI will create entirely new professions and transform existing jobs rather than eliminate them completely. Others fear that many workers, especially those performing routine tasks, may be replaced faster than they can retrain. Unlike previous technological revolutions, AI is advancing at an unprecedented speed, leaving governments and education
systems little time to respond effectively. As a result, many individuals may face uncertainty about their careers and financial stability.
Education is another area strongly affected by AI. III Traditional teaching methods that emphasize
memorization may no longer meet the needs of future societies. Instead, students must develop skills such as creativity, communication, critical thinking, and adaptability — abilities that machines cannot easily replicate. If schools fail to modernize, future generations may possess academic knowledge but lack the flexibility needed in an AI-driven world. Consequently, education should encourage lifelong learning rather than preparing students for only one career path.
Furthermore, AI raises important philosophical questions about intelligence and humanity. IV If
machines can imitate human conversation, decision-making, and even artistic expression, society must reconsider what truly makes humans unique. The issue ultimately extends beyond technology into ethics, responsibility, and human identity. Although AI may continue to become more powerful, humans will still determine how it shapes the future.
Ultimately, AI should not be viewed merely as a replacement for human ability but as a tool that can support human progress when used wisely. The future will depend not only on what AI is capable of doing, but also on the values and decisions of the people who create and control it.
According to paragraph 1, AI _______.
options: exists only in science fiction movies
is already part of many aspects of modern life
completely replaces human creativity in every field
has caused all industries to become automated

part1.q:
Read the passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the best answer to each of the following questions from 20 to 29.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) has rapidly become one of the most influential technologies of the modern era. Once limited to science fiction, AI is now integrated into daily life, from virtual assistants and recommendation systems to medical diagnosis and autonomous vehicles. Supporters argue that AI increases efficiency, reduces human error, and improves quality of life. However, critics warn that the widespread adoption of AI may create serious ethical, economic, and social challenges. The debate surrounding AI is therefore not simply about
technology itself, but about how humanity chooses to use it responsibly.
At first, AI appears to offer enormous advantages. I By automating repetitive and time-consuming tasks, AI allows humans to focus on creativity, innovation, and complex problem-solving. In healthcare, for example, AI systems can analyze medical data faster than doctors in certain situations, potentially improving patient
outcomes. Yet, despite these benefits, concerns remain about the unequal distribution of technological power. Large corporations with access to massive amounts of data may dominate industries, while smaller businesses and workers struggle to adapt to the changing economy.
Experts also disagree about AI’s long-term effect on employment. II Some believe that AI will create entirely new professions and transform existing jobs rather than eliminate them completely. Others fear that many workers, especially those performing routine tasks, may be replaced faster than they can retrain. Unlike previous technological revolutions, AI is advancing at an unprecedented speed, leaving governments and education
systems little time to respond effectively. As a result, many individuals may face uncertainty about their careers and financial stability.
Education is another area strongly affected by AI. III Traditional teaching methods that emphasize
memorization may no longer meet the needs of future societies. Instead, students must develop skills such as creativity, communication, critical thinking, and adaptability — abilities that machines cannot easily replicate. If schools fail to modernize, future generations may possess academic knowledge but lack the flexibility needed in an AI-driven world. Consequently, education should encourage lifelong learning rather than preparing students for only one career path.
Furthermore, AI raises important philosophical questions about intelligence and humanity. IV If
machines can imitate human conversation, decision-making, and even artistic expression, society must reconsider what truly makes humans unique. The issue ultimately extends beyond technology into ethics, responsibility, and human identity. Although AI may continue to become more powerful, humans will still determine how it shapes the future.
Ultimately, AI should not be viewed merely as a replacement for human ability but as a tool that can support human progress when used wisely. The future will depend not only on what AI is capable of doing, but also on the values and decisions of the people who create and control it.
Which of the following best paraphrases the underlined sentence in paragraph 3?
options: AI is developing so quickly that institutions may struggle to keep up.
Governments have successfully adapted to AI development.
Previous technological revolutions occurred faster than AI.
Education systems have fully prepared students for AI.

Read the following leaflet and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the option that best fits each of the numbered blanks from 30 to 35.
🚀🚀 CAREER PROSPECTS AND TRENDS IN VIỆT NAM 🚀🚀
How to stay alive in the job market?
From 2025 onwards, career trends in Việt Nam will have strong fluctuations. Many professions may be eliminated, (30) ______ new job opportunities may open. Are you among the safe or the dangerous? These are essential skills you can learn to strengthen your position in the career world.
1. Ability to apply technological knowledge
Digital transformation is actively (31) ______ into all current services. By 2030, it is possible for 100% of businesses to optimize business results based on digital tools and platforms. If you do not have the knowledge and skills to meet this, you will definitely be fired.
2. Analytical and critical thinking
Analytical and critical thinking is a valuable skill in the (32) ______ of growing jobs involving algorithms and data science. We live in a world filled with information. The most effective people are those who can analyse, interpret, evaluate pros and cons, and deliver data-driven solutions.
3. Self-management and self-learning
More and more businesses are using outsourced human (33) ______, working remotely. Therefore, they need people with self-management skills, demonstrated through responsibility, high discipline and adaptability to change. In addition, (34) ______ technology knowledge also requires a lot of self-learning and management effort from employees.
4. Emotional Intelligence
Under the remote working environment, stress in personal psychology and internal communication will be more likely to arise. People with high emotional intelligence will be preferred by recruiters because they can easily adapt, collaborate, negotiate, and resolve conflicts effectively at work (35) ______ communication styles. In particular, emotional intelligence is also an irreplaceable machine.
(Adapted from Think 12 Student’s Book)
